title: Veil and Oath
premise: Ansel Vane, runaway apprentice of the hedge-witch Mother Hessel, has survived seven years in the Thornfell mountains by knowing every smuggler's road and trusting no one. When the old gods stir and begin answering prayers, the court beneath the mountain takes notice—and claims the soul of Wren, a dying child Ansel once swore to protect, as payment for a bargain struck by Wren's ancestors. To reclaim it, Ansel must ally with Serah, a disgraced oath-keeper hunting the same court, and descend through the thirteen turns of the waning moon into a kingdom where every debt is honored and every mercy is a trap. In the end, Ansel learns the soul was sold using their own name—Mother Hessel's final betrayal—and must choose between escaping with Wren's soul and shattering the court's claim on all the mountain's hidden children, trading their invisibility for a truth that will remake the Thornfell forever.
about_author: Oscar Pemberton is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy rooted in folklore, debt, and the quiet violence of forgotten places.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Smuggling moon-iron through the Thornfell passes, Ansel witnesses a shrine to a dead god flicker alight at a traveler's whispered prayer. The old gods are waking, and every smuggler on the mountain feels the roads shift beneath them. Emotional beat: unease—the comfortable invisibility Ansel has built for seven years begins to crack.

chapters.title: Wren's Fever
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel returns to the village of Lowmarsh and finds Wren, the child they secretly watch over, burning with a fever no herb can touch. The village priest whispers of a bargain made generations ago. That night, a figure of shadow and antler appears at Wren's window and names a price already paid. Emotional beat: dread and protectiveness.

chapters.title: What Mother Hessel Taught
chapters.summary: POV Ansel, with flashbacks. Desperate, Ansel returns to the witch's cottage they fled years ago, finding it abandoned but the wards still humming. Among Hessel's papers, Ansel discovers records of soul-bargains with the court beneath the mountain—and a ledger page bearing their own childhood name. Emotional beat: betrayal, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Serah. Serah Ironmark, stripped of her order for refusing to burn a god-touched village, tracks Ansel through the passes. She knows the way into the court beneath the mountain—and that the thirteenth turn of the moon is the only door. She offers alliance; Ansel offers distrust. Emotional beat: wary friction between loyalty and necessity.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. The two travel the deep smuggler roads, but the waking gods have changed them—paths loop, stones speak, and a river demands a memory as toll. Ansel pays with the memory of their mother's face, and Serah sees it happen. Emotional beat: grief, and the first fragile moment of trust between them.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Serah. They descend through the moon-door into the underground court, where every soul is collateral and every kindness is invoiced. Ansel bargains for Wren's soul before the Moon-Throne, but the court's steward reveals the contract's signer: Mother Hessel, in Ansel's name. Emotional beat: vertigo—the trap was built long before they arrived.

chapters.title: Debts of the Hidden Children
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Exploring the court's vaults, Ansel finds shelves of soul-jars bearing names from every village in the Thornfell—children sold by the desperate, the greedy, and the well-meaning. Wren's jar is not among them; it is held in the throne room as bait. Emotional beat: righteous fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Serah. The court offers Serah her oath and her honor restored if she abandons Ansel and takes Wren's place as steward. Torn between the order she lost and the truth she's found, she refuses—and is thrown into the dark with Ansel as the moon begins its final turn. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over redemption on the court's terms.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Climax. With hours left, Ansel invokes the waking old gods—whose prayers they've been unknowingly carrying as a smuggler of sacred moon-iron—and the mountain itself wakes. Ansel shatters the Moon-Throne's ledger, voiding every contract, while Serah holds the steward's host at bay. Ansel takes Wren's soul and the court begins to crumble. Emotional beat: sacrifice and defiance.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. They surface as the moon completes its turn, Wren's fever broken and the old gods' shrines burning across the Thornfell. Ansel can no longer hide—the gods know their name, and so do the villagers. Standing with Serah and Wren at the rebuilt shrine, Ansel accepts a new oath: to be seen, and answer. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging.
